bugs.title: Subcommands (task/status/cache/inspect/artifacts/validate-state) resolve plan/ & PRD.md against the invocation dir, not the repo root — §9.8.7/§9.8.9 acceptance criteria fail
bugs.description: The headline §9.8 feature ("run from anywhere") is only half-wired. The §9.8.3 strategy is a single process.chdir(repoRoot) in main() AFTER parseCLIArgs() returns, on the theory that "every existing resolve('PRD.md')/resolve('plan')/process.cwd() site [becomes] correct with zero per-site changes" and that "all subcommands benefit automatically" (§9.8.7). This premise is FALSE for subcommands: each subcommand is a Commander .action() handler that runs DURING program.parse(process.argv) (src/cli/index.ts:853), i.e. INSIDE parseCLIArgs() and therefore BEFORE main()'s chdir. So their process.cwd() is still INVOCATION_CWD, and every bare resolve('plan')/resolve('PRD.md') resolves against the directory the user typed the command in. Only the `config` subcommand was patched — it explicitly calls resolveRepositoryRoot(process.cwd(), ...) in its own action handler (src/cli/index.ts:608). The other six were not. This violates (1) §9.8.9 "hack launched from src/, docs/, or any nested subdirectory resolves PRD.md, plan/, .hack, and .env at the repository root exactly as a root-launched run does"; (2) §9.8.7 which explicitly enumerates "hack task/status, hack artifacts, hack cache, hack inspect, hack validate-state, hack config" as automatic beneficiaries; and (3) §9.8.5/§9.8.9 "Any operational invocation of hack (including ... hack task ...) from outside any git repository exits 1 with a single actionable 'not a git repository' message naming the invocation directory and the --repo-root remediation." It also undermines the §5.3 breakdown-in-progress feature: `hack status` run from a subdirectory during an in-progress breakdown yields a scary "No sessions found" error instead of the calm notice, because plan/ resolves to the wrong place.
bugs.reproduction: Reproduce from a subdir (repo at /tmp/hack-subdir-test with plan/001_abcdef123456/tasks.json + .prd_hash present at the root): `cd /tmp/hack-subdir-test/src/deep/nested && hack status` → prints `ERROR: Task command failed: No sessions found` (exit 1), even though the session exists at the repo root and `hack status` from the repo root prints `Using main tasks: 001_abcdef123456/tasks.json` (exit 0). Reproduce outside any repo (/tmp/hack-test-nogit): `hack task` → `Task command failed: No sessions found` (exit 1) instead of the required "not a git repository / --repo-root" message; `hack validate-state` → `Failed to validate PRD exists at /tmp/hack-test-nogit/PRD.md` (resolving PRD against the invocation dir); `hack cache`/`hack inspect`/`hack artifacts` → "No session(s) found". Only `hack config show` correctly prints `No .git entry found at or above ...`. Synergy: `cd src/deep/nested && hack status` during breakdown (session dir exists, no tasks.json) → scary "No sessions found" instead of the §5.3 calm notice.
bugs.location: src/cli/index.ts:512-513 (artifacts action: resolve('plan')/resolve('PRD.md')); src/cli/index.ts:571-572 (cache action); src/cli/index.ts:638 (taskAction used by .command('task')@834 and .command('status')@844); src/cli/commands/inspect.ts:147-148 (InspectCommand default planDir=resolve('plan')); src/cli/commands/validate-state.ts:86-87 (ValidateStateCommand default); src/cli/commands/artifacts.ts:173-174 and src/cli/commands/cache.ts:70-71 (command-class defaults). The correct pattern to mirror is src/cli/index.ts:608 (config action calls resolveRepositoryRoot + chdir).

bugs.title: Config validation/secrets errors render via the scary default catch arm with a full stack trace, inconsistent with the clean single-message arms
bugs.description: PRD §9.7.6/§9.7.7 frame .hack secrets/type/range/enum/BOM/parse failures as user-facing misconfigurations that must surface as actionable startup errors mirroring the §9.2.7 fail-fast philosophy ("a misconfigured .hack must not surface as a deep runtime error mid-pipeline"). The messages themselves are correct and actionable, but they are rendered through main()'s DEFAULT catch arm (`console.error('\n❌ Fatal error in main():', error)` at src/index.ts:421), which appends the full Error stack trace. This is inconsistent with the dedicated clean arms for NotARepositoryError, AuthPreflightError, HarnessProviderMismatchError, and UnsupportedHarnessError, each of which prints a single `❌ <message>` line and exits. A user who typos `[tasks_lock] poll_ms = -5` or accidentally commits `[auth] zai_api_key` gets a stack trace into hack-config.js internals rather than the one-line actionable message the spec intends. Separately, the `config` subcommand's own try/catch (src/cli/index.ts:618) wraps even a NotARepositoryError in logger().error() with a request-id banner (`ERROR: [uuid] [CLI] Config command failed: <msg>`), so the one subcommand that DOES resolve the repo root still does not render the §9.8.5 "single actionable message" cleanly.
bugs.reproduction:
In a git repo with a valid PRD.md, create `.hack` containing `[tasks_lock]
poll_ms = -5`, then run `hack --dry-run`. Output: `
❌ Fatal error in main(): Error: [tasks_lock] poll_ms in <path>/.hack: -5 is out of range (expected integer in [1, +∞]).` followed by a 4-line stack trace through validateFieldValue → validateHackTier → loadHackConfig → main. Same for a secrets error (`[auth] zai_api_key = "..."` in committable .hack) and a BOM. Contrast: `hack --repo-root /tmp/notgit --dry-run` prints only `
❌ --repo-root path ... does not contain a .git entry.` (no stack) via the dedicated NotARepositoryError arm. Also: outside a repo, `hack config show` prints `ERROR: [<uuid>] [CLI] Config command failed: No .git entry found ...` (request-id banner) rather than a clean `❌` line.
bugs.location: src/index.ts:421 (default catch arm); src/cli/index.ts:618 (config action catch via logger().error). A typed error class + dedicated main().catch() arm (mirroring NotARepositoryError) would render these cleanly.

bugs.title: Relational constraint commit.retry_delay_cap_ms >= commit.retry_delay_ms is documented but not enforced
bugs.description: PRD §9.7.5 schema reference specifies `[commit] retry_delay_cap_ms` as "int ≥ retry_delay_ms" (the exponential-backoff cap must be at least the base delay). The validation schema (HACK_CONFIG_SCHEMA) validates retry_delay_cap_ms only as `int >= 0`, so a config with `retry_delay_ms = 200000` and `retry_delay_cap_ms = 100` — both individually valid integers — is accepted despite violating the documented relational constraint. The gap is acknowledged in a code comment ("The relational commit.retry_delay_cap_ms >= commit.retry_delay_ms cross-key check is a DOCUMENTED GAP (P2.M2 may harden)"), but §9.7.7 lists type/range mismatches as hard errors that must abort at startup, and the cross-key range is part of the §9.7.5 schema. Impact is low (a cap below the base delay merely prevents the doubling from ever applying), but it deviates from the spec table and is currently silently accepted.
bugs.reproduction: Create `.hack` containing `[commit]\nretry_delay_ms = 200000\nretry_delay_cap_ms = 100`, then run `hack config validate` — it reports "Configuration is valid." (exit 0) instead of flagging cap < delay. Both values pass the per-key `int >= 0` check; no cross-key comparison runs.
bugs.location: src/config/hack-config.ts — HACK_CONFIG_SCHEMA commit.retry_delay_cap_ms field spec (min: 0 only); validateFieldValue has no cross-key relational path. The acknowledging comment is inline in the HACK_CONFIG_SCHEMA block.

summary: Rigorous end-to-end testing of the §9.8 (repo-root), §9.7 (.hack config), and §5.3 (breakdown-in-progress) delta against the PRD. The repo-root RESOLVER itself is correct (worktree .git-file detection, nearest-ancestor nesting, --repo-root override, INVOCATION_CWD vs default-path semantics all pass), and the .hack loader is excellent (secrets policy, type/range/enum validation, three-tier precedence, env-over-file, BOM rejection, masked debug trace, CLI-only-key application incl. negated booleans, tracked-.hack.local warning, and hack config init/show/validate/path all work correctly). The breakdown-in-progress detection is correct when run from the repo root. However, the §9.8.3 "single bootstrap chdir benefits all subcommands automatically" premise is empirically FALSE: subcommands execute as Commander action handlers DURING parseCLIArgs(), before main()'s chdir, so 6 of 7 subcommands (task/status/cache/inspect/artifacts/validate-state) resolve plan/ and PRD.md against the invocation directory. Only `config` was patched. This breaks the §9.8.7/§9.8.9 acceptance criteria (run-from-anywhere + actionable not-a-repo message) for those subcommands and undermines §5.3 when invoked from a subdirectory. Two additional minor issues: .hack validation errors render with a scary stack trace instead of the clean single-message arms, and the documented retry_delay_cap_ms>=retry_delay_ms relational constraint is unenforced. All 110 delta unit tests and 37 integration tests pass (they test the resolver and loader in isolation, not the subcommand action-handler timing).
recommendations: Primary fix for BUG-001: resolve the repo root + chdir at the very start of EACH subcommand action handler (mirror the config handler at src/cli/index.ts:608), OR move the chdir to run during/before program.parse() (e.g. a program.hook('preAction') that resolves+chdirs for every command including subcommands). Re-run the §9.8.9 acceptance criteria from a subdir for all six subcommands after the fix.

Add an integration test that runs each subcommand from a nested subdirectory and asserts it resolves plan/PRD.md at the repo root — the current test suite tests the resolver in isolation and missed the action-handler timing gap.

For BUG-002, introduce a typed HackConfigError and a dedicated main().catch() arm (and have the config/other subcommand catch arms detect NotARepositoryError and render it cleanly) so misconfigurations print a single actionable line without a stack trace.
For BUG-003, add a post-validation cross-key check: if both commit.retry_delay_ms and commit.retry_delay_cap_ms are present, throw when cap < delay (§9.7.7 hard error).
